notes.title: General Information
notes.summary: Describes the Saudi Arabian Oil Company, headquartered in Dhahran, formed on November 13, 1988 by Royal Decree No. M/8 with a history dating to the 1933 concession. Under the Hydrocarbons Law (Royal Decree No. M/37, December 20, 2017) all hydrocarbons are the property of the Kingdom and the Government has sole authority to set maximum production and the maximum sustainable capacity; the amended Concession Agreement effective December 24, 2017 has a 40-year initial term, extendable by 20 years and potentially a further 40 years. Share capital is SAR 90,000 million divided into 242 billion shares after bonus issues in 2022 and 2023. Following the December 2019 IPO (3.45 billion shares, 1.73%), transfers of 4%, 4% and 8% of shares to PIF and its wholly-owned companies (2022-2024) and the June 11, 2024 secondary offering of approximately 1.7 billion shares (0.7%), the Government retains an 81.48% direct shareholding; the Company acquired 137.6 million shares from the Government for SAR 3,750 million as treasury shares. The financial statements were approved by the Board on March 3, 2025.
notes.investorRelevance: Establishes the Government's 81.48% direct shareholding, the 16% transferred to PIF-related entities since 2022, and the Concession Agreement under which the Kingdom owns all hydrocarbons and sets production limits - the foundation for assessing control and the sovereign relationship.

flag.text: The Government remains the controlling shareholder with an 81.48% direct stake after the June 11, 2024 secondary offering, and under the Hydrocarbons Law it has sole authority to set the Company's maximum production and maximum sustainable capacity.

notes.title: Material Accounting Policy Information and Significant Judgments and Estimates
notes.summary: Sets out the accounting policies applied in preparing the consolidated financial statements under IFRS as endorsed in the Kingdom and SOCPA pronouncements, prepared under the historical cost convention except for items measured at fair value. The most significant judgments relate to interests in subsidiaries, joint arrangements and associates, acquisition fair values, asset recoverability, lease terms, taxation, provisions, post-retirement obligations and functional currency. The USD is the Company's functional currency with SAR presentation at USD 1.00 = SAR 3.75; production royalties follow a progressive scheme of 15% up to $70 per barrel, 45% above $70 and 80% above $100. IFRS 18 becomes effective January 1, 2027 and has not been early adopted; no 2024 amendments had a material impact.

subnotes.title: Basis of preparation
subnotes.summary: IFRS as endorsed in the Kingdom and SOCPA standards, historical cost except investments in securities, derivatives, certain trade receivables/payables and plan assets at fair value.

subnotes.title: Significant accounting judgments and estimates
subnotes.summary: Lists the key judgment areas and notes that climate-change and energy-transition assumptions (net-zero Scope 1 and 2 ambition by 2050) are embedded in price, margin and growth estimates.

subnotes.title: New or amended standards
subnotes.summary: No material 2024 amendments; IFRS 18 (effective January 1, 2027) is being assessed and has not been early adopted.

subnotes.title: Principles of consolidation, acquisition and equity accounting
subnotes.summary: Subsidiaries consolidated on control, joint operations recognized line by line, joint ventures and associates equity accounted; acquisition method with goodwill allocated to cash-generating units.

subnotes.title: Intangible assets
subnotes.summary: Goodwill not amortized but tested annually; brands 10 to 22 years, franchise/customer relationships 5 to 25 years, software 3 to 15 years.

subnotes.title: Exploration and evaluation
subnotes.summary: Successful efforts method: exploratory well costs capitalized pending evaluation, written off when no commercial quantities are found.

subnotes.title: Property, plant and equipment
subnotes.summary: Cost less depreciation; straight-line or unit-of-production for oil and gas properties; useful lives from 2 to 54 years by asset class.

subnotes.title: Impairment of non-financial assets
subnotes.summary: Recoverable amount is the higher of fair value less costs of disposal and value in use; key assumptions are prices, volumes, costs, margins and discount rates.

subnotes.title: Leases
subnotes.summary: Right-of-use assets within PP&E and lease liabilities within borrowings, discounted at the incremental borrowing rate; short-term and low-value leases expensed.

subnotes.title: Investments and other financial assets
subnotes.summary: Classification at FVPL, FVOCI or amortized cost; provisionally priced trade receivables measured at fair value; expected credit loss impairment.

subnotes.title: Derivative instruments and hedging activities
subnotes.summary: Commodity derivatives held for trading through net income; interest rate swaps and currency forwards designated as fair value or cash flow hedges.

subnotes.title: Income tax and zakat
subnotes.summary: Current tax under the 2004 Tax Law, deferred tax by the liability method, zakat per ZATCA; Pillar Two temporary exception applied; the 20% Downstream rate continues to be applied.

subnotes.title: Inventories
subnotes.summary: Lower of cost and net realizable value; FIFO for hydrocarbons and chemicals, weighted average for materials and supplies.

subnotes.title: Due from the Government
subnotes.summary: Price equalization compensation and the Government guarantee of past-due receivables from Government-related entities, settled by offset against taxes.

subnotes.title: Cash and cash equivalents
subnotes.summary: Cash and highly liquid investments with original maturities of three months or less.

subnotes.title: Assets classified as held for sale
subnotes.summary: Measured at the lower of carrying amount and fair value less costs to sell, not depreciated.

subnotes.title: Treasury shares
subnotes.summary: Deducted from equity at the consideration paid including transaction costs.

subnotes.title: Financial liabilities
subnotes.summary: Derivatives and provisionally priced trade payables at FVPL; borrowings and other payables at amortized cost.

subnotes.title: Borrowing costs
subnotes.summary: Expensed except costs directly attributable to qualifying assets, which are capitalized.

subnotes.title: Post-employment benefit plans
subnotes.summary: Defined benefit plans valued annually by independent actuaries using the projected unit credit method, remeasurements through OCI; defined contribution costs expensed.

subnotes.title: Share-based compensation
subnotes.summary: Equity-settled awards measured at grant-date fair value; cash-settled awards remeasured each balance sheet date; recognized over the vesting period.

subnotes.title: Provisions and contingencies
subnotes.summary: Decommissioning provisions recognized for Upstream wells when drilled; Downstream decommissioning generally not recognized due to indeterminate settlement dates.

subnotes.title: Functional and presentation currency
subnotes.summary: USD functional currency, SAR presentation; the SAR has been fixed to the USD since 1986 and convenience translations use USD 1.00 = SAR 3.75.

subnotes.title: Revenue recognition and sales prices
subnotes.summary: Revenue recognized when control transfers; provisionally priced contracts recorded at estimated final price with later adjustments through revenue.

subnotes.title: Other income related to sales
subnotes.summary: Taxable Government compensation for revenue forgone under domestic regulated pricing, recorded as due from the Government.

subnotes.title: Production royalties
subnotes.summary: Progressive royalty on crude production: 15% up to $70 per barrel, 45% above $70 and 80% above $100, expensed and tax deductible.

subnotes.title: Research and development
subnotes.summary: Development costs with probable future benefits capitalized; other R&D expensed.

subnotes.title: Dividends
subnotes.summary: Provided when declared and no longer at the Company's discretion.

subnotes.title: Earnings per share
subnotes.summary: Basic EPS on net income attributable to ordinary shareholders over weighted average shares excluding treasury shares; diluted EPS adjusts for dilutive potential shares.

notes.investorRelevance: Defines the fiscal and structural ground rules: the progressive royalty scheme (15%/45%/80% at $70 and $100 per barrel), USD functional currency with the SAR peg, Government price-equalization compensation, and the control and joint-control judgments that determine which entities are consolidated.

notes.title: Financial Risk Management
notes.summary: Covers market (foreign currency, price, interest rate), credit and liquidity risk managed by a central treasury, with derivatives used only for risk management. A 5% move in listed equity prices would change OCI by SAR 622 million (2023: SAR 669 million) and a one percentage point change in interest rates would change pre-tax income by SAR 605 million (2023: SAR 1,281 million). Net debt was SAR 78,078 million at December 31, 2024 against net cash of SAR 102,753 million in 2023, taking gearing to 4.5% from (6.3)% on total borrowings of SAR 319,290 million and total equity of SAR 1,651,355 million. Casualty risk retention is SAR 3,301 million per loss event with insurance of SAR 4,388 million above retention. Financial assets at fair value totalled SAR 175,423 million (2023: SAR 142,270 million), of which SAR 146,864 million is Level 3, mainly provisionally priced trade receivables of SAR 128,101 million; Level 3 investments in securities rose to SAR 15,093 million from SAR 10,051 million.

Earnings before interest, income taxes and zakat were SAR 772,296 million (2023: SAR 865,037 million): Upstream SAR 801,047 million, Downstream a loss of SAR (10,998) million (2023: profit SAR 21,184 million) and Corporate SAR (21,830) million. Cash capital expenditures rose to SAR 188,890 million (2023: SAR 158,308 million), SAR 147,135 million of it Upstream. In-Kingdom external revenue was SAR 954,139 million and out-of-Kingdom SAR 683,160 million, including SAR 190,011 million originating from the USA; non-current operating assets were SAR 1,500,218 million In-Kingdom and SAR 223,942 million outside.

An impairment charge of SAR 10,370 million (2023: SAR 3,110 million), mainly on plant, machinery and equipment of certain domestic and international downstream facilities, was recognized following revised cash flow projections, with the recoverable amount of SAR 68,417 million determined on value-in-use at pre-tax discount rates of 8.3% to 11.6%; a further write-down of SAR 1,070 million was recorded. notes.title: Intangible Assets

The annual impairment test of the SAR 99,116 million goodwill from the SABIC acquisition, allocated to Downstream, found no impairment using 10-year value-in-use projections, a 2.25% terminal growth rate and a pre-tax discount rate of 11.0% (2023: 9.9%); the SAR 18,140 million SABIC brand was tested at 10.1% (2023: 9.1%) with no impairment. notes.title: Income Taxes and Zakat
notes.summary: The Company pays 50% income tax on most activities and 20% on Downstream and non-associated gas activities; the 20% Downstream rate, effective January 1, 2020, was conditional on separating Downstream into wholly-owned subsidiaries by December 31, 2024, failing which Downstream would be retroactively taxed at 50%, and an extension to December 31, 2030 is in progress and expected to be granted. Total income tax and zakat expense was SAR 383,588 million (2023: SAR 433,303 million) on income before tax of SAR 782,010 million, including current Kingdom tax of SAR 371,648 million and foreign taxes paid of SAR 3,193 million. The obligation to the Government fell to SAR 71,951 million (2023: SAR 82,539 million) after payments of SAR 176,523 million by the Company and SAR 188,642 million settled against amounts due from the Government. Net deferred tax liabilities were SAR 132,710 million; unrecognized deferred tax assets of SAR 17,113 million relate to SAR 68,705 million of unused losses. Saudi tax filings through 2019 were accepted, no significant claims are known, and no material Pillar Two exposure was identified.

notes.title: Post-employment Benefits
notes.summary: Saudi Aramco sponsors funded and unfunded defined benefit pension and other post-employment (mainly medical) plans, primarily in the Kingdom. The net position moved to a net benefit asset of SAR (499) million (2023: liability of SAR 1,486 million), comprising a pension surplus of SAR (8,693) million and a medical and other benefit liability of SAR 8,194 million, presented as non-current assets of SAR 27,365 million and non-current liabilities of SAR 26,866 million. Benefit obligations were SAR 72,600 million (pension) and SAR 103,542 million (other) against plan assets of SAR 81,293 million and SAR 95,348 million (total SAR 176,641 million). Discount rates rose to 5.6% (pension) and 5.8% (other), producing remeasurement gains of SAR (2,081) million and SAR (3,555) million in OCI; a 0.5% rise in the health care cost-trend rate would add SAR 8,546 million to obligations. The new Social Insurance Law effective July 3, 2024 had no material impact and 2025 employer contributions are estimated at SAR 2,760 million.

notes.title: Contingencies
notes.summary: Beyond ordinary-course disputes expected to have no material effect, Saudi Aramco discloses several guarantees. For Sadara's SAR 37,280 million senior debt restructured in 2021 (grace period to June 2026, maturity extended to 2038), the Company and Dow guarantee up to SAR 13,875 million of principal and interest in proportion to ownership, cover interest shortfalls until June 2026 and SAR 1,875 million of working capital shortfall in 2030, and have a SAR 1,500 million subordinated revolver (unutilized) plus letters of credit of SAR 169 million and SAR 152 million. For Petro Rabigh, the Company and Sumitomo each undertake to fund 50% of scheduled Rabigh II debt-service shortfalls until June 2032, SAR 5,625 million of shareholder revolving facilities were fully drawn (a phased waiver was agreed in August 2024), and the Company provided SAR 3,000 million of equity bridge loans and guaranteed a further SAR 1,655 million maturing December 20, 2027. The Company guaranteed SAPCO's 30% share of equity bridge loans (approximately SAR 800 million plus SAR 347 million of other guarantees) for the 2.6 gigawatt Al Shuaibah solar projects costing SAR 8,919 million, and provided SAR 816 million of guarantees for the 5.5 gigawatt Haden, Muwayh and Al-Khushaybi projects costing SAR 12,042 million. Other guarantees for affiliates total SAR 1,855 million (2023: SAR 1,863 million).

notes.title: Investments in Affiliates and Securities
notes.summary: Describes 2024 and 2023 portfolio transactions. Saudi Aramco acquired 100% of Chilean fuels retailer Esmax on March 1, 2024 for SAR 1,373 million (net assets SAR 1,096 million, goodwill SAR 255 million; post-acquisition revenue SAR 7,796 million), following the March 1, 2023 purchase of Valvoline's global products business for SAR 10,338 million (goodwill SAR 410 million). It agreed on August 7, 2024 to buy a further 22.5% of Petro Rabigh from Sumitomo for SAR 2,632 million, taking its stake to 60% with completion expected in the second quarter of 2025, alongside matching capital injections and a phased waiver of SAR 5,625 million of shareholder loans (SAR 1,935 million recognized in 2024). Other investments include a 40% stake in Gas & Oil Pakistan for SAR 279 million, SAR 195 million plus SAR 969 million in the MidOcean LNG associate, a 30% interest in the HAPCO refinery and petrochemical complex in China (construction cost SAR 43,000 million, Aramco equity share SAR 4,315 million with SAR 976 million undrawn), a 50% stake in Blue Hydrogen Industrial Gases closed on January 27, 2025, and a 10% stake in HORSE Powertrain for SAR 2,576 million. The 2023 acquisition of 10% of Rongsheng Petrochemical for SAR 12,767 million was recorded as a SAR 6,399 million FVOCI investment and a SAR 5,932 million asset for the long-term agreement to supply 480,000 bpd of crude oil to ZPC.
